replies.body: No. The default test task already uses non-preview mode, so the explicit override was redundant. Removed in f43c3c2.

threads.body: [Testing] The removed gauge used to assert the summary maximum, while the replacement assertion only checks that the gauge is absent. Assert `hasMax(4)` on the histogram point so the promised maximum remains covered for distribution summaries.
threads.hunk:
@@ -62,21 +62,7 @@ void testMicrometerDistributionSummary() {
                                         .hasAttributesSatisfyingExactly(
                                             equalTo(stringKey("tag"), "value"))
                                         .hasBucketBoundaries(NO_BUCKETS))));
-    assertMaxGauge(
-        testing(),
-        "testSummary.max",
-        metric ->
-            metric
-                .hasName("testSummary.max")
-                .hasDescription("This is a test distribution summary")
-                .hasDoubleGaugeSatisfying(
-                    gauge ->
-                        gauge.hasPointsSatisfying(
-                            point ->
-                                point
-                                    .hasValue(4)
-                                    .hasAttributesSatisfyingExactly(
-                                        equalTo(stringKey("tag"), "value")))));
+    assertNoMaxGauge(testing(), "testSummary.max");

threads.body: [Testing] This now verifies only that the legacy gauge disappeared, but not the advertised replacement: the histogram point's maximum. Add a `hasMax(42)` assertion to the histogram point so a regression that disables histogram min/max would not silently discard this value.
